How large is each part of a misfit?

Source: R/localize_update.R
localize.size.Rd

Gives the size of the four parts of localize.update on the risk scale, for frozen predictions on validation data. Four nested updates are fitted: the intercept update, the logistic recalibration, the flexible recalibration ns(eta, 4), and a revision that adds the main effects and the COV bases as one logistic model. The size of a part is the mean absolute change in predicted risk that its update makes beyond the simpler one, in percentage points.

Usage

localize.size(y, p, X, R = 200L, seed = NULL)

Arguments

y, p, X

as in localize.update.

R

number of chance draws for each part.

seed

optional integer, passed to set.seed() before the chance draws. The random number stream of the session is restored on exit.

Value

An object of class "gof_localize_size": a list with parts (a data frame with part, size, chance, excess and the noise interval lo, hi, in percentage points), calibration (the calibration intercept and slope with Wald 95% intervals) and ici (the integrated calibration index of Austin and Steyerberg, in percentage points).

Details

An update fitted to noise also moves the predictions, so each size comes with its chance level: the mean size over R outcome vectors drawn from the simpler update, under which the part is absent. excess is the size minus the chance level. The noise interval is the size minus the 97.5% and 2.5% points of the chance draws; under no misfit it contains 0 with probability of about 0.95. It is not a confidence interval for the true size: it only shows whether a size can be told from chance.

excess is a cautious lower measure, not an estimate of the true size. Every size is fitted with noise, so at moderate sample sizes the excess understates the true size, most of all for COV. A size that cannot be told from its chance level does not show that a part is absent; localize.update carries that evidence.

References

Ebrahim, E. K., Hussein, O. A. E.-A. and El-Kotory, A. (2026). Which update does a clinical risk model need? Localization of misfit in logistic risk models. Submitted. Reproduction materials: doi:10.5281/zenodo.24025418

Austin, P. C. and Steyerberg, E. W. (2019). The Integrated Calibration Index (ICI) and related metrics for quantifying the calibration of logistic regression models. Statistics in Medicine, 38(21), 4051–4065. doi:10.1002/sim.8281

See also

localize.update for the verdict.

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 500
X <- data.frame(x1 = rnorm(n), x2 = rnorm(n))
p <- plogis(-0.5 + 0.8 * X$x1 + 0.6 * X$x2)
y <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(-0.7 + qlogis(p)))   # overall risk too high
localize.size(y, p, X, R = 20, seed = 1)      # R = 20 to keep the example fast; use 200
#> 
#> Size of each part of the misfit, percentage points of risk
#> 
#>            size chance excess noise.lo noise.hi
#> INTERCEPT 12.77   1.65  11.11     9.59    12.37
#> SLOPE      1.21   1.15   0.07    -1.74     1.13
#> LINK       1.93   2.04  -0.12    -1.85     1.03
#> COV        4.48   3.58   0.90    -0.62     2.41
#> 
#> calibration intercept -0.697 (-0.913 to -0.482), slope 1.107 (0.849 to 1.366)
#> integrated calibration index 12.94
#>
